`sensitive_post_parameters`, given no names, marks every posted value as sensitive, which the error report hides while `settings.DEBUG` is `False` (`django/views/debug.py:SafeExceptionReporterFilter.get_post_parameters`).
No application of Django's ships the login view's template, `"registration/login.html"`; the documentation leaves it to the project (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).
A URL that fails gives an empty string, as no `"next"` does (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:RedirectURLMixin.get_redirect_url`).
The check is told in [The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md).

The mixin's default is `RedirectURLMixin.next_page` through `resolve_url`, a path or a URL pattern's name, and with no `next_page` it raises `ImproperlyConfigured`; `LoginView` and `LogoutView` replace it with their own (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:RedirectURLMixin.get_default_redirect_url`).
On a `"GET"`, `LoginView` renders `"registration/login.html"`, adding three entries to the form view's context (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView.get_context_data`).

`"site"` and `"site_name"` come from `get_current_site`: the sites application's current site when it is installed ([Content types, static files and the other contrib apps](../contrib.md)), and otherwise, as here, a `RequestSite` named after the request's host, harbour.example (`django/contrib/sites/shortcuts.py:get_current_site`).

On a `"POST"`, the form is `LoginView.authentication_form` if the view was given one, else `LoginView.form_class`, `AuthenticationForm` (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView.get_form_class`); `LoginView.get_form_kwargs` adds the request, which the form passes to `authenticate` and so to each authentication backend ([Authenticating: `authenticate` and the backends](authenticating.md)).
A valid one reaches `LoginView.form_valid`, which calls `login` with the form's user and redirects to `get_success_url` (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView.form_valid`).

Without a safe `"next"` that is `next_page`, else `LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL`, `"/accounts/profile/"` unless the settings say otherwise, a page Django does not provide (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView.get_default_redirect_url`).

Then `LoginView.dispatch` sends them to `get_success_url` as if the login had just succeeded, and raises `ValueError` if that URL is the request's own path, a redirect to itself (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView.dispatch`).
The check catches only a loop of one page; the documentation warns of a longer one, through `permission_required` without `raise_exception=True` (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).

`LogoutView.http_method_names` is `["post", "options"]`: `View.dispatch` hands any other method to `View.http_method_not_allowed`, a 405 whose `"Allow"` names the two (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.http_method_not_allowed`).
`LogoutView` and `logout_then_login` no longer log out on a `"GET"` (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`).

A target other than the request's full path is redirected to; when it is that path, the view answers the `"POST"` by rendering `"registration/logged_out.html"` (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:LogoutView.post`, `django/contrib/auth/views.py:LogoutView.get_default_redirect_url`).

`logout_then_login` is a function that calls a `LogoutView` whose `next_page` is the URL it is given, or `LOGIN_URL`; so it logs out only on a `"POST"`, and a safe `"next"` still wins (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:logout_then_login`).

So the view calls `update_session_auth_hash`, which gives the session a new key and the new hash so that, as its docstring says, the change does not log out the session it came from; then it redirects to `PasswordChangeDoneView` (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:PasswordChangeView.form_valid`, `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:update_session_auth_hash`).

`PasswordContextMixin` gives the templates of both views, and of the reset views, `"title"` from the view's title, a `"subtitle"` of `None`, and the extra context; the admin's templates show the title, and a subtitle when one is set, and the admin's password change is these views ([The site's own pages: the index, the login and `AdminSite.each_context`](../admin/site-views.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:PasswordContextMixin.get_context_data`, `django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/base.html`, `django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.password_change`).
